subtitle: International visitors · Year ending March 2026
Six Queensland regions in TRA’s national top 20 by visitor-nights
Circle size and shade = A$ spent per visitor-night · Unmarked regions are not covered

description: International spending per visitor-night in six Queensland tourism regions. Same population, measure and annual period as the preceding state choropleth. Regions selected because they appear in TRA Table 6 national top 20 ranked by visitor-nights; this is not a complete regional ranking, a hotel-price map, or evidence of visitor preferences. Circle area and a light-to-dark teal scale both encode the same spending per visitor-night. One shared legend displays matching circle areas and colours at A$50, A$100, A$150 and A$200; colour is not a separate measure; leader lines connect labels to region centroids.

usermeta.boundaries: TRA tourism regions, matching region names; simplified existing project geometry
usermeta.coverage: Six Queensland regions from the national top-20-by-nights table; unmarked regions are not zero.
usermeta.previous_figure_title: State averages reveal the broad spending pattern
usermeta.connecting_story: State averages show the broad picture. Looking within Queensland reveals how much international spending per night can differ between destinations.
usermeta.visual_encoding: Circle area: linear spending-per-night scale from 0 to A$220, symbol-size range 0 to 1100. Fill: opaque sequential light-to-dark teal for the same measure and numeric domain. The combined legend uses both scales, matching map symbols exactly. Darker/larger means more spending per visitor-night; unmarked regions are not zero.
usermeta.brisbane_connector: Brisbane’s display connector starts at the unchanged Brisbane symbol centre, turns north to the label latitude, then runs toward the label. It is drawn above the circles with a white halo and dark 1.5-pixel stroke so the source is visible. Sunshine Coast and Brisbane labels sit slightly higher; Gold Coast is unchanged.
